syntax.syntax_item: R = tessera.worley(sz, 'cells', c, 'feature', f, 'metric', m, 'seamless', tf)

param_input_item.param_description: Field size: a scalar for a square field, or a [rows cols] vector.
Number of feature points per axis (default 8).
Seed of the pseudo-random generator (default 0). The same seed reproduces the same field.
Output feature: 'f1' (default), 'f2', or 'f2-f1' for edge patterns.
If true, wrap feature cells on a periodic lattice (default false).

param_output_item.param_description: The generated field, a rows-by-cols double matrix normalized to [0, 1].

description.p: Generate Worley (cellular) noise: each pixel holds a feature-distance measurement from a jittered grid of points. F1 produces cellular blobs, F2 expands the second-nearest field, and F2-F1 emphasizes cell borders. Manhattan and chebyshev metrics create blockier pattern families. The result is normalized to [0, 1].

xmldoc.bibliography: M. Hendrikx, S. Meijer, J. van der Velden, A. Iosup, Procedural Content Generation for Games: A Survey, ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications and Applications 9(1), 2013. DOI 10.1145/2422956.2422957.

example_item.example_item_data: R = tessera.worley(256, 'cells', 12, 'seed', 1, 'feature', 'f2-f1', 'metric', 'chebyshev'); imagesc(R); axis image off
